deadline_pattern: Standing September 30 deadline (4:00 PM) each year for the following calendar year; the committee reviews at a posted public meeting at City Hall and council sets awards in the annual budget in November-December

annual_pool: Not published; the 2024 amended budget shows Motel/Hotel Tax Fund 105 totaling $468,236 (including fund balance) with a 2024 ending balance of about $79,700 after a $6,500 add for the Stampede hosting event
contact: Shannon Bland, Administrative Assistant (Hotel/Motel Committee staff), sbland@omakcity.com, 509-826-1170; Connie Thomas, City Clerk, 509-826-1170
notes: Omak calls it the Hotel/Motel Tax Fund program; applicants submit the city's Application for Hotel/Motel Funds (nonprofit, for-profit or public agency) to City Hall or by email by September 30, the Hotel/Motel Committee reviews at a public meeting at City Hall and recommends a list to council, and awards are adopted with the city budget and paid on reimbursement after the service is delivered. The city web page says funds are available to nonprofit agencies while the form itself offers a for-profit box. Omak Stampede is the dominant local event and received a mid-year $6,500 add in 2024 on committee recommendation. The 2026-2027 fund size and committee roster are not posted.

name: Arlington
tax_rate: 2% (state-shared basic lodging tax, per Arlington Times)
deadline_pattern: Applications posted by May 1 and due mid-June at 5:00 PM for the following calendar year (June 13, 2025 for 2026 funds); LTAC meets in August and council acts in September; the 2027-cycle date was not confirmed online
annual_pool: $185,000 available for 2026 (per 2026 application packet); $145,000 awarded in an earlier cycle against $230,995 requested
contact: Kristin Garcia, Finance Director, kgarcia@arlingtonwa.gov, 360-403-3431; Finance Department general line 360-403-3421
notes: Called the Tourism / Economic Development Grant and run by the Finance Department; one application per event, reimbursement only, request capped at 75% of project cost with a 25% minimum match, no salaries or giveaways, and projects must be inside city limits. For 2026 the committee met August 12, 2025 and council voted September 15, 2025, cutting SkyFest from the recommended $39,960 to $20,000 and keeping Hometown Holidays at $46,960, with the balance spread to the Farmers Market, Fourth of July, Street Fair and Summerdaze. Scoring favors events drawing visitors from 50+ miles, documented room nights, and packages with the five named Arlington hotels; projects funded three or more years running must show measurable growth.

name: Clarkston
deadline_pattern: Packet posted in September; proposals due mid-October at 5:00 PM (October 13 in the 2024 packet); LTAC public review tentatively the first week of November; council decides with the budget
annual_pool: 2025 awards reported at about $180,000: Visit Lewis-Clark Valley $145,000, Asotin County Family Aquatic Center $25,000, Valley Vision $10,000; 2027 fund projection not published
contact: Jeremy Walkup, Councilmember and Lodging Tax Committee member, council2@clarkston-wa.com, (208) 830-7548; Rachel Frost, City Clerk/Treasurer, City Hall (509) 758-5541
notes: Clarkston runs a Lodging Tax Funding Request process each fall; the 2027 Lodging Tax Packet and a scoring tool were posted on the City Clerk forms page in September 2026 but the PDFs could not be opened from this session, so the 2027 deadline is unconfirmed. The bulk of the fund goes to the regional DMO Visit Lewis-Clark Valley ($145,000 in 2025), leaving a small share for other applicants; the aquatic center got $25,000 after asking for $70,000. Applications require original plus six copies, a nonprofit registration, business license, itemized budget, and winners sign a Municipal Services Contract with insurance naming the city. Priorities are overnight stays in Clarkston and Asotin County lodging, visitors from outside 50 miles, and a track record. Council was also exploring a Tourism Promotion Area in June 2026, and lodging tax collections were reported up 52% year over year in mid-2025 on cruise ship traffic.

notes: Chewelah runs a small annual lodging tax grant through its online Form Center; the City Council Finance Committee serves as the LTAC, reviews applications in early December and council awards before the end of December. Awards totaled $31,250 for 2025 and $36,500 for 2026, well above annual collections of about $20,000, drawn from a fund balance of about $71,000. Activities must take place in Chewelah or exclusively promote Chewelah, free and low-cost public events are prioritized, partnerships and volunteer involvement are weighted, grants are reimbursed after a post-event report, and recipients must file a results report within 60 days. A rate increase from 3% to 4% was tabled in April 2026 until 2027.
